newsitem.title: DENMARK: Ansaldo signs Copenhagen Metro contract.
newsitem.headline: Ansaldo signs Copenhagen Metro contract.

text.p: Italian electromechanical group Ansaldo Trasporti, a world leader in transportation signalling systems, signed on Thursday a 450 billion lire ($300 million) contract to build and provide track, signalling, automation and trains for the new Copenhagen Metro.

The order was signed with Oerestadsselskabet, which is jointly owned by Copenhagen Municipal Council and Denmark's Finance Ministry with construction work expected to take three to four years and the Copenhagen Metro due to open around the year 2000.

The deal covers the design, construction, supply and installation in the city of a completely automatic urban metro system with 15 km (nine miles) of track and 15 stations, Ansaldo said in a statement.

Also included in the contract is the supply of 19 fully automatic driverless minimetro vehicles, designed to travel 3.1 million km (1.9 million miles) per year carrying 35 million passengers, Ansaldo said.
Tunnelling work is not embraced by the order.
The contract was signed in the presence of Ansaldo president Bruno Musso and Copenhagen mayor Jens Kramer Mikkelsen.

The project involves the linking by minimetro train of the city centre of Copenhagen with Oerestad, a new town to be built on the southern island of Amager, with further possible extensions at a later juncture.
